deviation_opinions.mechanism: src/scan/materialize.ts deletes Cargo.toml.orig, .cargo-ok, .cargo_vcs_info.json from the extracted .crate before git add/commit, dodging cargo-1.93's exit-101 abort ('invalid inclusion of reserved file name Cargo.toml.orig') seen live on rand_core@0.6.4
deviation_opinions.opinion: ACCEPTABLE with a documented tradeoff. The scrub removes exactly the files that break cargo 1.93's reserved-name gate; none of them carry repository-residue signal the T-scan is designed to catch — Cargo.toml.orig is the pristine pre-rewrite manifest (residue lives in authors/hosts/paths, which live in the scanned Cargo.toml), .cargo-ok is a build-progress marker, .cargo_vcs_info.json records the upstream git commit (provenance metadata, not sandbox residue). Same for the .cargo-ok/.cargo_vcs_info drop. The alternative (fail closed on every such crate) would make crates: scanning unusable — a worse outcome for the fail-closed gate than a documented, deterministic envelope reduction. HOWEVER: the scrub is a step AWAY from scan-what-was-shipped purity: a malicious crate could hide a build-only hook in Cargo.toml.orig and count on it being stripped. Recommended hardening (not blocking): log the removed file names + sha256 in the scan report or quarantine them under the sandbox instead of deleting, so the evidence is preserved for forensics; and assert the scrub only applies to those three exact names.

deviation_opinions.topic: gemspec-less gem fails closed at exit 2
deviation_opinions.mechanism: rubygems materialize unpacks data.tar.gz but does not require a gemspec; the rubygems channel then fails (exit 2) when the gem is gemspec-less
deviation_opinions.opinion: ACCEPTABLE per fail-closed doctrine, and the right call. A gem without a gemspec cannot be structurally verified: gemspec is where install-time behavior (executables, extension build scripts, runtime dependencies, and the metadata a T-scan keys its rules on) is declared. Falling back to data-only inspection would silently scan a structurally uninspectable artifact and produce a confidence the artifact doesn't merit — precisely the 'green light on an unverifiable input' failure mode border exists to prevent. Exit-2 with a one-line cause is correct. If the ecosystem ever ships legitimately gemspec-less gems, the fix is an explicit operator opt-in flag (e.g. --allow-gemspec-less), not silent data-only fallback.

deviation_opinions.mechanism: fetch.ts uses an ASCII-safe UA string; test asserts undici rejects non-ASCII header values
deviation_opinions.opinion: ACCEPTABLE and correct — undici throws on non-Latin-1 header values; the ASCII-only UA is the minimal compliant fix and carries no residue-relevant information loss.
